html:
The Battle of Legnica was fought on 9 April 1241 near Legnica in Silesia, where a Mongol force destroyed the army of Duke Henry II the Pious, which included Polish knights, German settlers and members of military orders.

It was a wing of the great Mongol invasion of Europe, sent to keep the Poles from helping Hungary. The Mongols had already burned Kraków. They used feigned retreats and smoke to break the knights. Henry was killed and his head was paraded on a spear. Two days later the main Mongol army crushed the Hungarians at Mohi. The Mongols did not stay, but Poland, split among quarrelling dukes, was raided again. Legend says the bugle call from Kraków's St Mary's Church breaks off mid tune in memory of a trumpeter shot by a Tatar arrow.
